entities.name: Amyloid-beta precursor protein
observations: The 753-residue query sequence has 83.5% identity and 100% coverage to reviewed Takifugu rubripes APP (UniProt O93279), supporting strong identification as APP.

Sequence contains an N-terminal signal peptide, APP_N and APP_Cu_bd domains, a Kunitz/BPTI inhibitor domain, APP_E2 domain, amyloid-region motifs, one type-I membrane helix, and a short cytosolic tail.
Predicted topology: large N-terminal luminal/extracellular ectodomain and short C-terminal cytosolic domain.
The cytosolic tail contains a YENPXY motif near the C terminus, consistent with clathrin-mediated internalization and adaptor-protein interactions.
The protein is acidic overall: calculated molecular weight about 84.9 kDa, pI about 4.83, and charge at pH 7 about -51; mature glycosylated/processed forms may differ.
APP functions as a neuronal cell-surface receptor/adhesion and signaling molecule and is processed into soluble APP, amyloid-beta peptides, and C-terminal fragments.
Reported localization includes plasma membrane, ER, Golgi, secretory and cytoplasmic vesicles, clathrin-coated pits, early/recycling endosomes, and neuronal projections.

Biological roles supported by homolog annotations include neurite growth, neuronal adhesion, axonogenesis, synaptic processes, intracellular trafficking, and signaling through protein-protein interactions; exact roles are context- and isoform-dependent.

entities.name: Amyloid-beta peptide
observations: The APP ectodomain/transmembrane region contains the conserved amyloidogenic segment that can be released as amyloid-beta after beta- and gamma-secretase processing; this is a processing potential, not evidence of disease in the source sample.

entities.name: APP processing
observations: APP can undergo alpha-, beta-, and gamma-secretase processing, producing soluble ectodomains, amyloid-beta peptides, and intracellular C-terminal fragments.

entities.name: Endomembrane system
observations: APP trafficking and maturation involve the ER, Golgi, plasma membrane, secretory vesicles, clathrin-coated pits, and early endosomes.
